limits: Exact directEnemy source fairyA, CEL enFairy(Clone), motion renderer enFairy01 and source renderer 121395 only. This archive grants no inheritance to another fairy source or renderer topology.

The native pass action preserved enemy HP58 and reduced hero HP from 995 to 991 while recording AttackProf, fairy_attackProf, damage 4 and Damaged. This is sampled native gameplay under the survival fixture, not a balance claim.

The first ordinary zero-focus attack used the native bluntSmithHammer without a skill cap or damage fixture and produced native Dodge with enemy HP unchanged at 58, followed by fairy_dodge. Two later fairy_attackProf sequences each dealt 4 damage to the hero, changing hero HP from 991 to 983.

The second ordinary zero-focus native hammer attack reduced Moonreed from 58 to 55 HP with recorded damage 3, a Damaged response and fairy_damaged. A later fairy_attackProf recorded zero damage and native Dodge against the hero.
The explicit KillSingle fixture reduced Moonreed from 55 to 0 HP with recorded native 1000 damage and a Death trigger. It is fixture death evidence, not ordinary lethal gameplay.

The source has m_DoRagdoll false. The animator remains enabled while fairy_die persists from frame 26 through frame 119. The two recorded nonkinematic rigid bodies are inactive break props and receive no ragdoll credit.

All four captures retain the requested 120 frames. The exact renderer remains active, enabled, reported visible and identity-stable through all 480 frames. The sampled animated death remains present through frame 119, but this boundary does not establish general corpse lifetime, cleanup causality or final disposal.
One guarded native Collect action succeeded and strict Ready succeeded at dungeon level 0, room 2, with one active Ready button.

Thirty selected original PNGs were reviewed. Native effects, foreground hero overlap, the small native presentation, fixed-camera perspective, loot UI and late depth blur limit fine inspection in stated frames; the remaining 450 capture PNGs are preserved by hash but were not individually reviewed.

The profile preserves native CEL scale 1.0. Its Standard matFairyA material uses the authored moonreed_basecolor.png main texture with emission disabled, zero emission color and no emission map. This route does not establish portrait pixels, other cameras, other resolutions or all-angle culling.

This isolated dungeon trial does not prove every fairy animation, collision, alternate materials, long-session resource lifetime, inheritance to another fairy source, full campaign progression or finished-art acceptance.

selectedPNGs.observation: Moonreed is fully visible in settled native fairy_cIdle. The custom sylph has a coherent hovering silhouette with four pale peach wings, a teal and dark body, long lower limbs and a curled red antenna; its small native presentation limits fine surface inspection, but no native replacement mesh is visible.

During native fairy_attackProf, Moonreed rises above a bright pink ground burst. Its head, torso, wings and long lower silhouette remain connected and recognizable, while the native glow and camera movement restrict color judgment near the lower body.

The proficiency attack reaches the hero while Moonreed remains a coherent airborne figure above the native ground effect. Bright attack light, the foreground hero and impact effects limit detailed inspection; the associated native action records 4 damage against the hero.

Moonreed has recovered to fairy_cIdle after the proficiency attack. The full custom silhouette is intact and centered, although residual lighting makes the wings appear brighter than in the settled opening frame.
The first ordinary zero-focus attack attempt begins with Moonreed intact at 58 HP in fairy_cIdle. The full small custom model is visible before the player acts.
At the opening of native fairy_dodge, the foreground hero covers most of Moonreed. The visible wings and head remain attached, but this overlap prevents a complete pose or surface judgment.
The native DODGED label appears while Moonreed holds a displaced fairy_dodge pose behind the target cell. Its wings, torso and lower limbs remain coherent, and enemy HP remains 58.
After fairy_dodge, Moonreed has returned to its centered hover. The authored four-wing silhouette and palette are again readable with enemy HP unchanged at 58.
A later native fairy_attackProf lifts Moonreed above the bright pink ground effect. The body and all four wings remain attached and readable despite the strong central glow.
The first later proficiency attack lands for 4 damage against the hero. Moonreed stays recognizable above the native effect, while impact light and the foreground hero limit detailed review.
Moonreed is back in a stable hover after the first later attack. The model is fully framed and coherent while the native ATTACK DOWN result remains on the hero.
A second later fairy_attackProf begins from the same intact authored model. The bright ground burst masks the lower tip, but the head, torso and wing arrangement remain connected.

The second later attack records another 4 damage against the hero. Moonreed remains visibly intact above the diminishing native glow, though the damage graphic and combat lighting limit surface inspection.

The first attempt ends with Moonreed restored to its complete fairy_cIdle silhouette at 58 HP. The visible hero damage and ATTACK DOWN text belong to the sampled native enemy attacks, not the player's dodged strike.
The second ordinary attack attempt begins with the same exact Moonreed binding intact at 58 HP. Its full small silhouette is visible before impact.

The ordinary hammer impact is dominated by a bright native sphere and foreground hero. The displayed 56 HP is an intermediate UI state, so this frame establishes the event boundary but cannot prove the final damage or a complete hit pose.
Native fairy_damaged is active at the final 55 HP with the recorded 3-damage label. Moonreed is partly behind the hero, but its head, wings and body remain connected in the hit response.

The later fairy_damaged pose remains coherent while overlapping the hero. The visible wings, torso and lower body do not separate, but the foreground player prevents an unobstructed full-pose judgment.
Moonreed has recovered from fairy_damaged to the centered hover at 55 HP. The complete authored silhouette is visible again.
A later native fairy_attackProf again raises the complete custom sylph above the native glow. The model remains connected while the effect limits lower-body detail.
The hero's native DODGED result leaves hero HP unchanged. Moonreed is fully visible in recovery lighting with the four-wing silhouette still intact; this frame does not represent enemy damage.
The second attempt ends at the next native player decision with Moonreed intact in fairy_cIdle at 55 HP. The combat UI partly covers the hero while the enemy remains fully visible.
The explicit KillSingle capture begins with the exact custom sylph intact at 55 HP in fairy_cIdle. This is a separate death fixture and the attack-selection panel covers only the hero.

The telemetry-selected native Death trigger coincides with a large impact sphere and foreground hero. Moonreed is almost fully obscured, so this frame establishes the fixture boundary but not the death pose.
Native fairy_die begins with the animator still enabled. The 1000-damage label, hero and effects cover much of Moonreed, while the visible wings and body remain part of the authored model.

Moonreed is horizontal in the early animated fairy_die fall. The four wings, torso and long lower silhouette remain connected as the model moves toward the floor; this is animation rather than ragdoll motion.
The animated death has placed Moonreed prone on the floor. The authored body and wings remain visibly coherent while the 1000-damage label and hero occupy the foreground.

After the combat HUD clears, the prone custom sylph remains visible on the dungeon floor through this bounded frame. This sample establishes only capture persistence, not general corpse lifetime or cleanup behavior.
The native Victory loot panel and depth blur cover nearly all of the fallen model. This frame supports the successful loot flow but cannot provide a useful surface or death-pose review.

The final bounded frame still presents the native Victory collection panel with heavy depth blur. Telemetry retains the exact active, enabled and reported-visible renderer through this frame, but the image does not establish corpse readability, cleanup timing or final disposal.
